Definition: of uncertain affinity; there; by extension, thither:--there, thither(-ward), (to) yonder (place).
BiblicalUsage: There is the word of place, and the New Testament uses it to put the reader on the scene. There was a marriage in Cana of Galilee, and there were six waterpots of stone standing there, and Peter finds a man named Aeneas lying on a bed for eight years there in Lydda. James warns against telling a poor man to stand there while the rich man sits in a good place, because there can be a place of honour or a place of shame.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God is there, wherever there is, because the wedding, the sickbed, and the assembly are all places He visits. My position is that no place is too ordinary for Him to show up in.
